name: Apollo 11 - Tranquility Base
description: First crewed lunar landing (1969), lunar module Eagle in southwestern Mare Tranquillitatis, a flat basaltic mare plain near the equator.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Apollo 11 LM), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283, 92-103 (LRO-derived Apollo coordinates, ME frame)

name: Apollo 12 - Ocean of Storms
description: Second crewed landing (1969), a pinpoint landing in Oceanus Procellarum next to the Surveyor 3 probe; mare basalt plain.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Apollo 12 LM, lon 336.5781 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938

name: Apollo 14 - Fra Mauro
description: Crewed landing (1971) in the Fra Mauro highlands, hummocky terrain thought to be Imbrium basin ejecta.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Apollo 14 LM, lon 342.52806 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938

name: Apollo 15 - Hadley-Apennine
description: First J-mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle (1971), between Hadley Rille and the Apennine Mountains at the edge of Mare Imbrium.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Apollo 15 LM), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938

name: Apollo 16 - Descartes Highlands
description: Only Apollo landing in the central lunar highlands (1972), Descartes region, with rover traverses to North Ray and Stone Mountain.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Apollo 16 LM), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938

name: Apollo 17 - Taurus-Littrow
description: Last crewed landing (1972), a valley between massifs at the southeastern edge of Mare Serenitatis.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Apollo 17 LM), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Apollo Landing Sites, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunar_sites.html

name: Luna 9
description: First soft landing on the Moon (1966) and first surface panoramas, in western Oceanus Procellarum. Coordinates are the older NSSDCA estimate (0.01 deg precision).
sources: NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (Luna 9, 295.63 E), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Luna 13
description: Soft lander (1966) in Oceanus Procellarum that measured soil density with a penetrometer. Coordinates are the older NSSDCA estimate (0.01 deg precision).
sources: NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (Luna 13, 297.95 E), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Luna 16
description: First robotic sample return (1970), from Mare Fecunditatis near the equator.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Luna 16), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
description: Delivered Lunokhod 1, the first remotely driven rover on another world (1970), in northwestern Mare Imbrium.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Luna 17, lon 324.99837 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Luna 20
description: Robotic sample return (1972) from the Apollonius highlands north of Mare Fecunditatis.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Luna 20), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
description: Delivered the Lunokhod 2 rover (1973) inside Le Monnier crater on the eastern edge of Mare Serenitatis.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Luna 21), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Luna 24
description: Last Soviet lunar mission and sample return (1976), drilling about 2 m into Mare Crisium.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Luna 24), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Soviet Lunar Missions (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunarussr.html

name: Surveyor 1
description: First US soft landing (1966), inside the Flamsteed P ring in Oceanus Procellarum.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Surveyor 1, lon 316.6602 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Surveyor Program (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/surveyor.html

name: Surveyor 3
description: Lander (1967) in Oceanus Procellarum, later visited by the Apollo 12 crew who returned parts of it to Earth.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Surveyor 3, lon 336.5820 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Surveyor Program (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/surveyor.html

name: Surveyor 5
description: Lander (1967) in Mare Tranquillitatis that made the first chemical analysis of lunar soil, near the later Apollo 11 site.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Surveyor 5), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Surveyor Program (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/surveyor.html

name: Surveyor 6
description: Lander (1967) in Sinus Medii near the center of the near side; first liftoff and short hop from the lunar surface.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Surveyor 6, lon 358.5725 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Surveyor Program (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/surveyor.html

name: Surveyor 7
description: Only Surveyor in the highlands (1968), on the ejecta blanket north of the young crater Tycho.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Surveyor 7, lon 348.4873 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938
NSSDCA, Surveyor Program (landing time), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/surveyor.html

name: Chang'e 3 / Yutu
description: First Chinese soft landing (2013), with the Yutu rover, in northern Mare Imbrium.
sources: LROC, Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (Chang'e 3, lon 340.4883 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/938

name: Chang'e 4 / Yutu-2
description: First landing on the far side (2019), in Von Karman crater inside the South Pole-Aitken basin; no direct Earth visibility, relayed via the Queqiao satellite.
sources: LROC, Topographic Map of the Chang'e 4 Site, https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1100
NASA M2M-30044 Lunar Surface Data Book, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20250002845/downloads/M2M-30044%20Lunar%20Surface%20Data%20Book%20Baseline_Final.pdf

name: Chang'e 5
description: Sample return (2020) from young mare basalts near Mons Rumker in northern Oceanus Procellarum.
sources: LROC, First Look: Chang'e 5 (lon 308.0839 E), https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/1172
NSSDCA, Chang'e 5 (landing time about 15:13 UT), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2020-087A

name: Chang'e 6
description: First sample return from the far side (2024), near the southern edge of the Apollo basin inside South Pole-Aitken; no direct Earth visibility.
sources: NASA Lunar Discovery and Exploration Program Update 2025 (41.63 S, 153.99 W), https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/cds/researchers/nac/pac/2025/20-%20ESSIO-Lunar%20Update%20-%20LDEP_TAGGED.pdf
NASA, LRO Spots China's Chang'e 6 Spacecraft on Lunar Far Side, https://www.nasa.gov/missions/lro/nasas-lro-spots-chinas-change-6-spacecraft-on-lunar-far-side/

name: Chandrayaan-3 - Shiv Shakti Point
description: First landing at high southern latitude (2023), Vikram lander and Pragyan rover in the highlands about 600 km from the south pole.
sources: LROC, Chandrayaan-3 Landing Site, https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1314
NSSDCA, Chandrayaan 3 (landing time 12:33 UT), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2023-098A

name: SLIM - near Shioli crater
description: Japanese precision-landing demonstrator (2024) on a sloped crater rim near Shioli crater; landed within about 100 m of its target but tipped onto its nose.
sources: LROC, JAXA SLIM Landing, https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/1358
JAXA, SLIM press conference 2024-01-25, https://www.isas.jaxa.jp/en/outreach/announcements/files/SLIM-pressconf-20240125.pdf

name: IM-1 Odysseus - Malapert A region
description: First commercial lunar landing (2024), near the south pole in a degraded crater; the lander came to rest tilted on its side.
sources: NASA, LRO Images Intuitive Machines' Odysseus Lander (80.13 S, 1.44 E), https://www.nasa.gov/missions/lro/nasas-lro-images-intuitive-machines-odysseus-lander/

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 - Mons Latreille
description: First fully successful commercial landing (2025), in Mare Crisium about 4 km from Mons Latreille; operated through a full lunar day.
sources: NSSDCA, Blue Ghost Mission 1, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=BLUEGHOST

name: IM-2 Athena - Mons Mouton
description: Southernmost landing so far (2025), on the Mons Mouton plateau near the south pole; the lander ended on its side in a small crater.
sources: LROC, IM-2 Landing Region, https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1401
NASA, LRO Views IM-2 on Moon's Surface, https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/nasas-lunar-reconnaissance-orbiter-views-im-2-on-moons-surface/

name: Artemis candidate region - Peak near Cabeus B
description: NASA candidate region for the first Artemis crewed landing near the south pole, on a peak next to the crater Cabeus B. APPROXIMATE location: center of the IAU feature Cabeus B (crater), not the region center, which NASA does not publish; the region can be several km away.
sources: NASA, NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions (2024-10-28), https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-artemis-iii-moon-landing-regions/
IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Cabeus B (crater) (center -82.26, -54.58), https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/8058

name: Artemis candidate region - Haworth
description: NASA candidate region for the first Artemis crewed landing near the south pole, on the rim area of Haworth crater, which hosts permanently shadowed terrain. APPROXIMATE location: center of the IAU feature Haworth (crater), not the region center, which NASA does not publish; the region can be several km away. NOT REPRESENTATIVE: this point is on the crater floor (about -3.3 km), not on the rim, so it gets no Sun and no Earth; do not read its metrics as those of the landing region.
sources: NASA, NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions (2024-10-28), https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-artemis-iii-moon-landing-regions/
IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Haworth (crater) (center -87.45, -5.17), https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/14502

name: Artemis candidate region - Malapert Massif
description: NASA candidate region for the first Artemis crewed landing near the south pole, on the Malapert Massif, a mountain facing the Earth. APPROXIMATE location: center of the IAU feature Mons Malapert, not the region center, which NASA does not publish; the region can be several km away.
sources: NASA, NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions (2024-10-28), https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-artemis-iii-moon-landing-regions/
IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Mons Malapert (center -85.98, -1.67), https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16338

name: Artemis candidate region - Mons Mouton Plateau
description: NASA candidate region for the first Artemis crewed landing near the south pole, on the flat top of Mons Mouton (IM-2 landed on it in 2025). APPROXIMATE location: center of the IAU feature Mons Mouton, not the region center, which NASA does not publish; the region can be several km away.
sources: NASA, NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions (2024-10-28), https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-artemis-iii-moon-landing-regions/

name: Artemis candidate region - Mons Mouton
description: NASA candidate region for the first Artemis crewed landing near the south pole, on the slopes of Mons Mouton. APPROXIMATE location: center of the IAU feature Mons Mouton, not the region center, which NASA does not publish; the region can be several km away.

name: Artemis candidate region - Slater Plain
description: NASA candidate region for the first Artemis crewed landing near the south pole, on a plain near Slater crater, close to the pole. APPROXIMATE location: center of the IAU feature Slater (crater), not the region center, which NASA does not publish; the region can be several km away.
